name: Alibaba Cloud ACK (Harbor backend)

modes.label: ACK cluster runtime
modes.note: Pods on ECS worker nodes: price = ECS node rates (see alibaba-ecs card) for whole nodes; ACK requires worker nodes of at least 4 vCPU / 8 GB. ACK itself adds the Pro cluster fee.

modes.label: ACK pods on virtual nodes (ECI), per vCPU/GiB
modes.note: ECI list rate (docs give no region; 'Prices displayed on the purchase page and in bills take precedence'). Billed from Pending (image pull) to Succeeded/Failed on requested, not used, resources. Economy vCPU $0.015264/h. 30 GiB temp storage free per pod, extra ~$0.000000093/GiB-s. ack-virtual-node component is free; cluster fee (Pro $0.09/h or Basic free) still applies. Regional ECI vCPU quota varies by account history.

plans.name: ACK managed Pro
plans.note: USD 0.09 per cluster per hour x 730 h. Per cluster, not per sandbox; billed every hour the cluster is Running/Upgrading/etc. even with zero pods; first and last partial hour free; 'Prices may vary by region'. Can be offset by a resource package. Workers (ECS/ECI), API-server CLB, NAT gateway, EIP, disks billed separately.

plans.name: ACK managed Basic
plans.note: No cluster management fee; max 10 nodes/cluster, 1,000 serverless pods/cluster, 2 clusters/account, not raisable; docs say 'For personal testing or learning only'. All cloud resources still billed.

caveats: Harbor ACK is customer-managed Alibaba Kubernetes, distinct from Alibaba AgentRun/FC sandbox. Platform and underlying worker node/storage/network billing must be combined.
Not fully priceable in ENGINE_CARD: unknown USD resource rates or machine shape. Null is not zero; do not rank as a free provider.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

fleet.verification: Identity verification required before creating a cluster.
fleet.tiers: Basic: 2 clusters/account, 10 nodes/cluster, 10 node pools, 1,000 serverless pods/cluster (not adjustable; 'for personal testing or learning only'). Pro: 100 clusters/account; nodes/cluster Flannel 200 default (1,000 max) or Terway 5,000 default (50,000 max); 50,000 serverless (ECI) pods/cluster; increases via Quota Center. Underlying ECS on-demand quota 500 vCPU, spot 800 vCPU (ticket).
fleet.notes: Cluster/node ceilings are not a new-account machine entitlement: backing ECS/ECI quotas, network quotas and stock still bind. Do not multiply cluster maxima into default instances. ECI create rate: CreateContainerGroup token bucket burst 100, refill 20/s (ticket to raise); ECI regional vCPU quota 'Varies by account based on historical usage' (Quota Center). The cluster fee, API-server CLB and NAT are paid per cluster.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Volume snapshots help you back up and restore application data.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Disk-volume (PVC) snapshots only via Kubernetes VolumeSnapshot backed by ECS disk snapshots (billed as ECS snapshots); restore into a new PVC via dataSource, so new pods can start from it. No memory, no container rootfs. ECS worker-node disks can also be snapshotted via ECS. ACS Agent Sandbox (separate product) offers memory checkpoint and cloning.

egress_allowlist.quote: you can use network policies to control network traffic at the IP address or port level for specific applications in your cluster
egress_allowlist.note: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy (egress ipBlock rules) enforced by Terway eBPF (shared ENI mode only; 'ACK supports only standard Kubernetes network policies', no Calico/Cilium FQDN policies); ACK Pro GlobalNetworkPolicy via Poseidon; ECS/ECI security-group egress rules. No domain-level egress for plain ACK documented (ACS Agent Sandbox SecurityProfile does domain/URL rules).

ingress_rules.quote: Each network policy can contain a whitelist of source (ingress) rules.
ingress_rules.note: NetworkPolicy ingress rules (podSelector/ipBlock), ECS/ECI security groups, and choice of Service type (ClusterIP vs LoadBalancer/Ingress with CLB/ALB) decide which ports are exposed.

guest_firewall.quote: NET_ADMIN Perform network-related operations such as configuring interfaces and routing tables.
guest_firewall.note: Containers, not VMs: iptables inside the pod needs the NET_ADMIN capability added via securityContext (listed as supported for ECI pods; default containers lack it). Pods on ECS nodes follow standard Kubernetes capability rules. Rules apply to the pod's network namespace only.

secret_proxy.quote: ack-secret-manager syncs secrets from Key Management Service (KMS) to your Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) cluster as Kubernetes Secrets.
secret_proxy.note: Plain ACK: secrets reach the pod as Kubernetes Secrets (env/files), also via csi-secrets-store-provider. ACS Agent Sandbox's egress gateway has a SecurityProfile 'tokenTransformation' action ('API key injection, or Alibaba Cloud STS credential replacement and re-signing', HTTP/HTTPS with TLS termination) - a real first-party credential-injection proxy, but documented for ACS Agent Sandbox, not ACK.

volume_attach.quote: automatically creating and mounting a dedicated cloud disk for each application replica
volume_attach.note: Cloud-disk PVs via CSI (static/dynamic), also NAS, OSS, CPFS volumes.

volume_shared.quote: data sharing, enabling simultaneous read and write access by multiple pods
volume_shared.note: Read-write NAS (NFS) PVs with ReadWriteMany; OSS bucket mounts (ossfs) also available.

isolation.quote: ACK pods run as standard Kubernetes containers scheduled onto ECS worker nodes or ECI virtual nodes
isolation.note: Card top-level isolation is already 'container' (Kubernetes pods sharing the worker-node/ECI kernel). ECI virtual-node pods run in a lightweight per-pod sandbox but the product as a whole is modeled as container isolation, matching the card.

image_oci.quote: Deploy applications by using container images stored in Container Registry or any OCI-compatible registry
image_oci.note: Card already has custom_image: true. Pods are started from any Docker/OCI image, including customer-pushed images (ACR or external registries).

docker_inside.quote: ACK managed cluster nodes use containerd as the container runtime
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. ACK worker nodes and ECI pods run on containerd, not Docker; nested Docker daemons inside a pod require privileged/docker-in-docker workarounds that Alibaba does not document as a supported feature.

nested_virt.quote: NET_ADMIN Perform network-related operations such as configuring interfaces and routing tables.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Pods are containers (ECS containerd or ECI microVM sandboxes); no documented /dev/kvm passthrough or nested-virtualization capability for ACK pods.

desktop.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. ACK is a generic Kubernetes container platform, not a desktop/remote-GUI product.

browser.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No managed browser ships with ACK.

computer_use.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No screenshot/click desktop-driving API is part of ACK.

anti_bot.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. ACK is a Kubernetes runtime, not a browser/bot-automation product.

captcha_solving.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: you can use network policies to control network traffic at the IP address or port level for specific applications in your cluster
egress_ip_type.note: Pod outbound traffic is SNAT'd through a NAT Gateway or ECS/EIP, both datacenter Alibaba Cloud IPs; a NAT Gateway EIP is fixed/static unless changed by the customer.

ssh.quote: you can log on to ECS nodes by using SSH key pairs
ssh.note: ACK worker nodes are ECS instances reachable by SSH; individual pods are reached via kubectl exec, not SSH directly.

snapshot.quote: Volume snapshots help you back up and restore application data.
snapshot.note: Disk/PVC snapshots only (backed by ECS disk snapshots); no memory/process-state snapshot for plain ACK pods.

snapshot_auto.quote: Volume snapshots help you back up and restore application data.
snapshot_auto.note: Volume snapshots must be explicitly created via a VolumeSnapshot object/CronJob; there is no automatic checkpoint on pod stop/idle.

fork.quote: Volume snapshots help you back up and restore application data.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Kubernetes pods are declarative/replicated from a spec (ReplicaSet scaling), not cloned as a single running machine; there is no 'fork this pod' API.

fork_running.quote: Volume snapshots help you back up and restore application data.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no running-pod clone/fork capability documented.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Volume snapshots help you back up and restore application data.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; snapshots are disk-only, no memory/process state, and there is no fork/clone feature to carry it.

pause_resume.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
pause_resume.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Kubernetes pods are scaled to 0 replicas or deleted/recreated, not paused/resumed as a single machine with billing paused mid-state.

persistent_disk.quote: automatically creating and mounting a dedicated cloud disk for each application replica
persistent_disk.note: Cloud-disk PersistentVolumes survive pod restarts and reattach to rescheduled pods.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
auto_stop_idle.note: Kubernetes autoscaling (HPA/cluster-autoscaler) scales replica count based on load metrics; it is not a per-machine idle-timeout stop that plain ACK provides out of the box.

live_resize.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
live_resize.note: Standard Kubernetes pod resource requests/limits require a pod restart/reschedule to change; ACK docs do not advertise in-place CPU/RAM resize without recreating the pod.

agent_harnesses.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No coding-agent (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode) templates ship with ACK.

harness_api.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

own_agent_api.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. ACK has no first-party browser/computer-use/research agent product; that is Alibaba's separate ACS Agent Sandbox / AgentRun offering.

lang_python.quote: Deploy applications by using container images stored in Container Registry or any OCI-compatible registry
lang_python.note: Any language runtime is available by supplying a container image (e.g. official python images); not a managed out-of-the-box runtime, but fully supported via custom images.

lang_node.quote: Deploy applications by using container images stored in Container Registry or any OCI-compatible registry
lang_node.note: Any language runtime is available by supplying a container image (e.g. official node images); not a managed out-of-the-box runtime, but fully supported via custom images.

public_ipv4.quote: Each network policy can contain a whitelist of source (ingress) rules.
public_ipv4.note: Public exposure is via CLB/EIP bound to a Kubernetes Service (LoadBalancer type) or Ingress, giving a public IPv4 endpoint for the workload.

inbound_https.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
inbound_https.note: Ingress/CLB/ALB resources terminate HTTPS and route to pod ports; standard ACK ingress-nginx / ALB Ingress Controller documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: ACK supports only standard Kubernetes network policies
egress_http_rules.note: Card's own feature_evidence for egress_allowlist gives level 'ip': standard NetworkPolicy egress rules operate at IP/CIDR/port level, not HTTP method/path level; no domain/URL-level egress documented for plain ACK.

static_egress_ip.quote: you can use network policies to control network traffic at the IP address or port level for specific applications in your cluster
static_egress_ip.note: Outbound traffic can be routed through a NAT Gateway bound to a fixed EIP, giving pods a stable, static outbound IP.

macos.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. ACK node pools are Linux or Windows Server ECS instances; no macOS node type is offered.

arm64.note: ACK managed cluster creation supports Arm64 (Yitian) ECS instance types as node pool architecture.

self_host.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
self_host.note: ACK is a managed control plane hosted by Alibaba Cloud; the ACK service itself cannot be run on the customer's own infrastructure (the underlying Kubernetes upstream project can, but that is not this product).

open_source.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
open_source.note: ACK is Alibaba Cloud's proprietary managed Kubernetes service (control plane, console, integrations); it is built on the open-source Kubernetes project (Apache 2.0) but ACK itself is not open source.

soc2.note: Listed under Alibaba Cloud's compliance/trust center, which covers ACK as an Alibaba Cloud service.

hipaa.quote: HIPAA (United States) US The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
hipaa.note: Alibaba Cloud lists HIPAA compliance support on its trust center compliance page.

sso.note: Alibaba Cloud CloudSSO provides SAML-based single sign-on for account/console access, applicable to managing ACK access via RAM/CloudSSO.

eu_data_residency.note: Alibaba Cloud operates a Germany (Frankfurt) region where ACK clusters and their data can be kept within the EU.

max_session_h.quote: Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) is a fully managed Kubernetes service
max_session_h.note: ACK clusters and pods run indefinitely until the customer stops/deletes them; there is no maximum session duration imposed by the platform.

wake_on_request.quote: Run serverless workloads on Kubernetes with request-based auto scaling, scale-to-zero, and canary releases. ... Knative Serving: Manages serverless workloads with application deployment, multi-version management, request-based auto scaling, canary releases, and scale-to-zero when there is no traffic.
wake_on_request.note: Via ACK Knative (Knative Serving/KPA): a service idled to zero pods is scaled back up when a new request arrives (request-based autoscaling). This is an optional add-on component, not default plain-ACK behavior, and applies at the pod/service level rather than to a whole worker VM.

mcp_server.quote: Alibaba Cloud's ack-mcp-server unifies container operations capabilities, enabling AI assistants and third-party AI agents to perform complex tasks via natural language through the MCP protocol, empowering container-native AIOps.
mcp_server.note: First-party MCP server for ACK cluster/container operations (cluster, node, workload, and pod management via natural language through MCP).
